title: Tor-independent localized comparison for an A-K-flat complex
statement: Let R,A,B,D be commutative rings, with R-algebra structures on A and B, and an E=A\otimes_R B-algebra structure on D. Assume \operatorname{Tor}_i^R(A,B)=0 for every i>0 [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Let Q be a cochain complex of A-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] that is K-flat over A, meaning that its total tensor with every acyclic A-complex is acyclic [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Assume D is flat over E [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For every base-derived tensor cohomology model M [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model], its specified canonical map D\otimes_E H^i(Q\otimes_R^L B)\to H^i(D\otimes_A Q) is an isomorphism for every i\in\mathbf Z. No boundedness or finiteness of Q, or flatness of A or B over R, is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08IB, lemma-compare-base-change, Tor-independent affine calculation; More on Algebra, Section 06Y5 and Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change

proof.text: Use the existing ModuleCat.hasFunctorialFlatResolution instance and its reduced resolution functor to obtain P -> X, where X is Q restricted to R, with P R-K-flat and augmentation s a quasi-isomorphism. Convert its kFlat predicate to the acyclic-tensor property via the homotopy-category quotient equivalence. Apply the K-flat scalar-extension counit theorem to M.derived, M.counit and M.universal at P.

Apply lem-pc-tor-independent-kflat-resolution-tensor to s to show that its ordinary extension to B is a quasi-isomorphism. In the naturality square of M.counit at the homotopy image of s, the derived image of s and the ordinary extension of s are isomorphisms after localization, as is the counit at P. Rewrite by this naturality equality and cancel the invertible derived image to prove the counit at X invertible.

Rewrite comparison_eq. The counit on cohomology and every other factor on its right side are isomorphisms, so the composite on the left is invertible. Cancel the exact-restriction homology isomorphism and reflect isomorphisms through restriction from A tensor_R B to B to obtain IsIso (M.comparison i). The model already supplies the E-linear map, so no independent action-naturality theorem is needed.

By the flat scalar-extension homology adjunct theorem, the adjunction transpose t of homologyMap ordinaryToLocalized followed by exact restriction is invertible. Apply injectivity of the scalar-extension homEquiv and its naturality in the source to localized_eq: localizedComparison equals extension of comparison followed by t. Extension preserves comparison isomorphisms, so this composite is invertible.

lean.statement:
theorem localizedComparison_isIso_of_torIndependent_kFlat
    {R A B D : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing D]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra (A ⊗[R] B) D]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} B)]
    (hTor : ∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i →
      IsZero (((CategoryTheory.Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj (ModuleCat.of R A)).obj
        (ModuleCat.of R B)))
    (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (hK : ∀ L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ, L.Acyclic →
      (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor L Q (MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor _)).Acyclic)
    (hD : Module.Flat (A ⊗[R] B) D)
    (M : BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A B Q D) :
    ∀ i : ℤ, IsIso (M.localizedComparison i)
